overview: Sukuna’s settings tune his Coercion charge and healing, ground-slam placement, and the camera during his second cursed-energy attack.
technicalOverview: Ryomen Sukuna (CP_020) has three populated unique rows. Row 0 drives the Coercion charge/heal and the shockwave from super cursed-energy hits. Row 1 places NormalAttack_1’s ground-slam point and the downward trace that snaps it to ground. Row 2 is the camera preset for charging/releasing CursedEnergyAttack_2 (Attack H). CP_020 has its own controller and twelve custom action types, but inherits shared base actions and camera helpers. No CP020-specific .inl is included.

CP_020.title: Coercion, stored heal, and super-attack shockwave
CP_020.overview: The main row holds the level threshold and heal multiplier for the Coercion charge, plus the start radius, end radius and duration of the shockwave from super cursed-energy hits. Generic row-0 readers exist, but the AI hold and steering reads were not traced to a CP020 caller.

0.label: Coercion heal multiplier; generic fallback timing
0.simple: With Coercion charged, 0.85 times damage taken is saved as later healing. The same number is a fallback restraint time if Sukuna receives projection sorcery with no damage row.
0.technical: UCP_020_ActionController::OnDamageReceived calls the base first, then requires IsCoercionCharged() and sets Status->PendingHealAmount = GetCharacterUniqueFloatValue(0,0) * Damage (0.85 * Damage here). OnDamageDealt adds a positive saved amount to current hit points only while the charge test still passes and IsHitPointEmpty() is false, then clears it; knockout clears it too. Shared ProjectionSorceryReceive uses GetOwnerUniqueFloat(0,0) as RestraintTime only when Request.DamageTableRow is null; a real damage row wins. Shared AI hold nodes use this as a base duration and base steering uses it as an angle divisor, but the traced CP020 behavior path selects different AI actions and no CP020 caller of steering was found.

1.label: Coercion charge level threshold
1.simple: Coercion charging is available at cursed-energy level 2 or higher while the cursed-energy disable timer is not running.
1.technical: IsCoercionCharged() first returns false when CursedEnergyDisabledTimeLeft > 0; otherwise it returns static_cast<float>(CursedEnergyLevel) >= GetCharacterUniqueFloatValue(1,0), so level 2 is included. The inlined twin IsCoercionCountReached() applies the same test in OnDamageDealt; the out-of-line copy serves controller slots 173/183. The BUFF_COERCION_CP_020 grant is separate: level 3, or level 4 when the previous level was not 3. A generic AI hold node multiplies this value by CursedEnergyLevel, but CP020 was not traced to that node.

2.label: Super shockwave starting radius
2.simple: Super cursed-energy hits start a shockwave at a 1000-unit radius around Sukuna.
2.technical: In OnDamageDealt, only when DamageRow->AttackType == EGameAttackType::SuperCursedEnergyAttack, GetCharacterUniqueFloatValue(2,0) is passed as StartRadius to AGameBattleManager::StartShockwave with the owner location as Center. StartShockwave uses it as the From value of a linear radius ease; initial destructible target collection uses EndRadius instead.

3.label: Super shockwave ending radius
3.simple: The super-attack shockwave expands out to 3000 units.
3.technical: GetCharacterUniqueFloatValue(3,0) is EndRadius. StartShockwave adds tickable, not-yet-broken destructible objects whose squared distance from the center is <= EndRadius * EndRadius (it skips only when greater), and uses the same value as the To value of the linear radius ease.

4.label: Super shockwave expansion duration
4.simple: The shockwave radius change takes 1 unit of engine time.
4.technical: GetCharacterUniqueFloatValue(4,0) is passed as Duration to StartShockwave, which calls Radius.Start(StartRadius, EndRadius, Duration, EEasingFunc::Linear, 2.0f, 2). The interpolator advances Duration by DeltaTime and completes when Elapsed >= Duration; no CP020-specific scaling is applied.

notes.text: The AI hold readers of row 0 are real shared code, but CP020 does not use those executors in the traced setup: CP040 (and CP050 for one variant) select the Hold nodes, while the base factory used by CP020 selects CursedEnergyAttack1/CursedEnergyAttack2.

Do not merge the level-3 Coercion buff with the level-2 heal threshold: the buff grant checks level 3 (or level 4 from a different previous level), while the heal path only checks >= the row-0 threshold and the disable timer.

CP_020_ATTACKA.title: NormalAttack_1 ground-slam placement
CP_020_ATTACKA.overview: Both ground and air NormalAttack_1 use this row: it puts the effect point ahead of Sukuna, then starts a downward trace above that point and snaps to the first hit.

0.label: Forward reach to the slam point
0.simple: The slam effect is aimed 300 world units ahead of Sukuna.
0.technical: FCP_020_NormalAttack_1 and FCP_020_NormalAttackAir_1 both call TCP_020_NormalAttack_1::UniqueAction. Offset starts as ZeroVector, Offset.X = GetOwnerUniqueFloat(0,1) = 300, the actor rotation rotates that offset, and it is added to owner location to make the effect/trace point. Y/Z stay zero. Both variants share this value; no other float in this row affects the point.

1.label: Downward trace start height
1.simple: The ground check starts 150 world units above the aimed point and traces down to it.
1.technical: When ShouldTraceGround() is true (always for CP020 NormalAttack_1), TraceStart = candidate point + UpVector * GetOwnerUniqueFloat(1,1) = +150 world units and TraceEnd is the candidate point. StateCondition_LineTraceMulti uses the shared shot-blocker object types; on a hit whose first result has |Distance| > 1e-8, the effect translation becomes Hits[0].ImpactPoint. The trace runs for both ground and air variants; only the later surface-effect gate differs.

notes.text: The ground variant also looks up the surface at the final point and plays a mapped effect; the air variant skips that step. This is a fixed virtual override, not another float in this row.
The spawned base effects are fixed ids (FX_CP_020_01101 ground, FX_CP_020_01111 air); no unique-float lookup selects them.

CP_020_ATTACKH_SHOOT_CAMERA.title: Attack H charge/release camera preset
CP_020_ATTACKH_SHOOT_CAMERA.overview: CursedEnergyAttack_2 saves the current camera mode and switches to camera mode 2 with this row when UniqueAction parameter is 0. The shared MakeUniqueCameraRequest helper reads indices 0-10 from row 2; index 6 is also reused when handing the camera back.

0.label: Camera offset X
0.simple: The camera is offset -150 along the gaze-space X axis.
0.technical: GetCharacterUniqueFloatValue(0,2) becomes Request.CameraOffset.X in FGameCharacterAction::MakeUniqueCameraRequest, which only fills the request for CameraMode == 2 (CP020 passes 2). Mode-2 code rotates the whole offset by gaze rotation before adding it to the eye base; -150 is the literal X component, not an inferred direction.

1.label: Camera offset Y
1.simple: The camera is offset -65 along the gaze-space Y axis.
1.technical: GetCharacterUniqueFloatValue(1,2) is stored in OffsetY and written to Request.CameraOffset.Y, part of the same rotated camera placement as index 0.

2.label: Camera offset Z
2.simple: The camera is offset 15 along the gaze-space Z axis.
2.technical: GetCharacterUniqueFloatValue(2,2) is stored in OffsetZ and written to Request.CameraOffset.Z before the mode-2 camera applies the rotated offset.

3.label: Maximum downward gaze angle
3.simple: The look-at point can sit up to 60 degrees below the eye line.
3.technical: GetCharacterUniqueFloatValue(3,2) becomes Request.LimitAngleDown. Mode-2 code compares AngleBetweenDegrees(gaze direction, horizontal gaze heading) against 60 when the gaze target is below the eye and clamps only when the angle is greater; equality is allowed.

4.label: Maximum upward gaze angle
4.simple: The look-at point can sit up to 30 degrees above the eye line.
4.technical: GetCharacterUniqueFloatValue(4,2) becomes Request.LimitAngleUp. The same clamp uses it when the gaze target is above the eye; the test is strictly greater-than.

5.label: Camera field of view
5.simple: The charge camera uses an 85-degree field of view.
5.technical: GetCharacterUniqueFloatValue(5,2) becomes Request.FieldOfView. ChangeCameraMode applies a new FOV only when it is > 0; 85 qualifies, and with the positive blend time at index 6 the FOV is interpolated rather than snapped.

6.label: Field-of-view blend time
6.simple: FOV changes take 0.2 time units; the same value blends the camera back to a 90-degree FOV on release.
6.technical: MakeUniqueCameraRequest writes GetCharacterUniqueFloatValue(6,2) to Request.FieldOfViewBlendTime, easing the 85-degree charge FOV over 0.2. It is read again in TCP_020_CursedEnergyAttack_2::FinishAttackEffects: only when the next action is AttackDefault and the camera is still in mode 2 does CP020 set FieldOfView = 90 with this blend time and restore SavedCameraMode. Positive blend time starts FovInterp; <= 0 would snap.

7.label: Field-of-view easing selector
7.technical: GetCharacterUniqueFloatValue(7,2) is cast to int32 and switched: 0 -> Linear, 1 -> EaseIn, 2 -> EaseOut, 3 -> EaseInOut, other values leave the request default. Here 0 is a read value selecting Linear, not an absent setting.

8.label: Gaze orbit yaw
8.simple: The gaze is orbited 5 degrees in yaw around the camera.
8.technical: GetCharacterUniqueFloatValue(8,2) becomes Request.OrbitYaw. Mode-2 code builds FRotator(OrbitPitch, OrbitYaw, 0) and, when non-zero, rotates the gaze around the camera before the final look rotation.

9.label: Gaze orbit pitch
9.simple: No extra pitch is applied to the gaze orbit.
9.technical: GetCharacterUniqueFloatValue(9,2) becomes Request.OrbitPitch and is the Pitch component of that FRotator. It is explicitly read even though zero here; the five-degree yaw from index 8 still makes the orbit rotator non-zero.

10.label: Camera roll
10.simple: No roll is applied by this camera request.
10.technical: GetCharacterUniqueFloatValue(10,2) becomes Request.Roll and is passed to SetViewTarget87 as the roll argument. The read happens even when the value is zero; zero means an unrolled view.

notes.text: The camera switch happens only for UniqueAction IntParameter 0; parameter 1 only sets the release flag. The previous camera mode is saved before the switch and restored on the guarded finish path.
This row is CP020’s CursedEnergyAttack_2 data. Other characters call the same MakeUniqueCameraRequest with their own indices, so equal field positions elsewhere are not evidence of shared values.

Row numbers are positional: Id_CharacterUnique is copied into UniqueRows in order and GetCharacterUniqueFloatValue is an unchecked UniqueRows[RowIndex]->FloatValue[ValueIndex] dereference. A zero float means the stored value is zero, not that the slot is unused.

CP020’s controller creates twelve action types (ground/air NormalAttack_1, four NormalAttack_3 variants, ground/air CursedEnergyAttack_1 and _2, and both ExtraAttacks); other types fall back to UGameCharacterActionController::CreateAction. That is why shared camera and projection-sorcery helpers matter here while other characters’ controllers do not.

No CP020-specific .inl is part of these reads: CP_020_ActionController.cpp includes its own headers and ordinary game headers, while row-2 camera requests are built by the shared FGameCharacterAction::MakeUniqueCameraRequest body.

Trap and shikigami readers were not assigned to these rows: FGameTrapAction::GetUniqueFloat forwards through a trap’s source interface and AGameShikigami::GetCharacterUniqueFloatValue reads shikigami rows from ShikigamiUniqueDataTables; neither is AGameCharacter’s CP_020 path.

Coercion healing is cleared on knockout, while reaching level 3 or above on revival can grant the Coercion buff; these are separate from the row-0 charge threshold and are not additional unique floats.
